metaData.originalTitle: 别让 AI 瞎猜了：用 Harness Engineering 终结无限返工
metaData.title: Stop Letting AI Guess: Ending Endless Rework with Harness Engineering
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the Harness Engineering methodology, which advocates preparing stable task entry points, execution foundations, tool boundaries, verification feedback, and result records for AI Agents, transforming AI from a one-time generation tool into a reliable collaborative executor within the R&D process.
metaData.summary:
Based on the practical experience of the iQiyi technical team, this article systematically elaborates on the concept, principles, and practical methods of Harness Engineering. The core argument is that while AI programming tools are powerful enough for local generation, stable delivery still relies on clear foundations, boundaries, verification, and records. The article compares traditional Prompt Engineering with Harness Engineering, pointing out that the former addresses 'how to articulate clearly in this round,' while the latter addresses 'how to consistently get it right within the project.'

The article details the composition of a minimum viable Harness, including five key elements: task constraints and rules, tool execution entry points, context and plan artifacts, permission control and failure recovery, and verification review and result recording. Through two case studies—frontend (Pencil → Storybook → real pages) and backend (docs → plan → verify → implementation)—it demonstrates how to engineer the collaboration pipeline.

The article also provides a path for implementation, starting with a lightweight Harness and progressing through three stages: enabling the Agent to find the entry point, allowing tasks to be reviewed and reused, and gradually mechanizing recurring issues. Finally, it offers criteria for determining applicability and includes an auxiliary initialization Prompt.

mainPoints.point: An Agent's reliability comes not only from model capabilities but also from engineering conditions.
mainPoints.explanation: For an Agent to stably participate in R&D, engineering conditions such as task entry points, execution foundations, tool boundaries, verification feedback, and result records need to be prepared in advance, rather than relying solely on the quality of model responses.

mainPoints.point: The core of Harness Engineering is migrating temporary context to stable project locations.
mainPoints.explanation: Move project context, task scope, implementation preferences, and verification methods out of the conversation and into repository files like AGENTS.md, docs, and plan, enabling information reuse and standardized collaboration.

mainPoints.point: Both frontend and backend scenarios can be broken down into three layers: the execution foundation layer, the state exposure layer, and the delivery implementation layer.
mainPoints.explanation: For the frontend, use Pencil and Storybook to fix structure and state respectively; for the backend, use docs and verify scripts to fix semantics and verification conditions. The Agent then fills in the implementation once the structure and state are clear.

mainPoints.point: Implementation should start with a lightweight Harness and progress in stages.
mainPoints.explanation: First, establish a unified task entry point and a repository entry map. Then, supplement complex task plans and reusable verification. Finally, upgrade high-frequency issues into lints, scripts, or CI gates.

keyQuotes: For an Agent to reliably participate in R&D, it cannot rely solely on model responses. The project needs to prepare task entry points, execution foundations, tool boundaries, verification feedback, and result records for it.
Prompt addresses how to articulate clearly in this round, while Harness addresses how to consistently get it right within the project.
AI can accelerate generation, but stable delivery still depends on clear foundations, boundaries, verification, and records.

The key to moving from Prompt Engineering to Harness Engineering lies here: not just pursuing a better model response in this round, but enabling the project itself to have a working method that supports the Agent in repeatedly taking over, verifying, and writing back.
